answer: A lone plume of activity earns nothing until peers co-sign it in the open meadow of shared task logs, forcing an attacker to fund and coordinate thousands of bonded personas. Sybil resistance here rests on a staked-identity ledge: each agent must lock a bond that decays unless it performs verifiable work, so spawning fake identities costs real capital per clone. Cheap throwaway accounts simply cannot climb the ledge, making mass fakery economically irrational. From sa0016's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
